description: We are ASTROCEA, a student team from Colegio Empresarial los Andes Facatativá, Colombia, passionate about space exploration, science, engineering, technology and innovation. We developed MARSHAB, an educational Mars mission simulator. Our team brings together creativity, research, programming and problem-solving skills. We welcome people interested in aerospace engineering, software development, science communication and space exploration.
summary:
MARSHAB is an educational Mars mission simulation developed by ASTROCEA in response to NASA Space Apps Challenge’s “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer.” Set in Jezero Crater, the game places players in a 30-sol mission where they explore the Martian environment, collect resources, build essential infrastructure, manage crew supplies, and complete mission objectives.
By combining exploration, construction, resource management, and real Mars mission references, MARSHAB transforms complex space exploration concepts into an interactive learning experience. Its in-game science database introduces players to robotic missions, spacecraft, and discoveries from Mars exploration.
MARSHAB aims to inspire future explorers by making space science more accessible and engaging, while encouraging curiosity, problem-solving, and systems thinking. Resource production and consumption values are educational estimates, not direct measurements of real Martian operations.
details: MARSHAB is a browser-based educational video game developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with a Canvas-based game environment. It places players in a 30-sol Mars mission set in Jezero Crater, where they explore the terrain, collect resources, discover real robotic missions, construct infrastructure, and manage the supplies of a simulated four-person crew. The game features an interactive map, astronaut controls, a resource management interface, construction mechanics, mission objectives, and an educational database about Mars exploration. Players must monitor oxygen, water, food, energy, and materials while completing tasks and progressing through the mission. MARSHAB benefits learners by transforming space exploration concepts into interactive decisions. Its intended impact is to encourage scientific curiosity, problem-solving, and systems thinking, while making Mars exploration more accessible to younger audiences. Its creative approach combines planetary exploration, colony construction, resource management, and real mission references in a single educational experience. During development, our team considered usability, gameplay progression, scientific accuracy, resource limitations, and the distinction between real mission information and educational assumptions. Resource production and consumption values are simplified estimates, not measurements of actual Martian operations. NASA missions and publicly available space science resources informed our research and educational content. References consulted included NASA's Mars mission records, Goddard's DOME Lab, NASA Mission Viz, and NASA software resources. These were research references, not software components claimed to be integrated into the game.
